```{r}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (
      file.exists(file.path(candidate, "renv.lock")) &&
        dir.exists(file.path(candidate, "audit"))
    ) {
      return(candidate)
    }
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) {
      stop("Could not locate the project root from: ", start)
    }
    candidate <- parent
  }
}

)

read_stage2 <- function(directory, filename) {

    stop("Missing Stage 2 report input: ", path)

  readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

styled_p <- function(value, significant) {
  displayed <- nh_p_value_display(
    as.numeric(value),
    as.logical(significant),
    na_label = "—"
  )
  ifelse(
    displayed$p_bold,
    paste0("**", displayed$p_display, "**"),
    displayed$p_display
  )
}

format_p_inline <- function(value, significant) {
  styled_p(value, significant)
}

add_independent_p_displays <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(
      raw_p_display = styled_p(.data$p_raw, .data$p_raw < 0.050),
      adjusted_p_display = styled_p(
        .data$p_adjusted_BH,
        .data$p_adjusted_BH < 0.050
      )
    )
}

audit_gt <- function(data, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  data |>
    gt() |>
    tab_header(
      title = md(title),
      subtitle = if (is.null(subtitle)) NULL else md(subtitle)
    ) |>
    opt_row_striping() |>
    tab_options(
      table.width = pct(100),
      data_row.padding = px(4),
      heading.align = "left",
      source_notes.font.size = px(11)
    )
}

primary_maximum <- contrast_source |>
  filter(.data$run_id == primary_run) |>
  slice_max(.data$female_to_male_shifted_ratio, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

format_clock_midpoint <- function(hour) {
  total_minutes <- round(hour * 60)
  sprintf("%02d:%02d", (total_minutes %/% 60) %% 24, total_minutes %% 60)
}

stopifnot(
```

::: {.callout-important title="Stage 2 author decision required"}
The approved H11-METHOD-001 through H11-METHOD-007 analysis is complete. The
primary near-eye result, complementary chest result, gap-timing-unaware
sensitivity, diagnostics, V0 comparison, and the authorised 50-resample
effect-size pilot are reported below. No production bootstrap, leave-one-site-
out refit, or reader-facing H11 notebook has been run. The final section lists
the decisions needed to proceed.
:::

## Question and implementation status

The signed preregistered hypothesis is:

> H11: Diurnal exposure patterns differ by sex.

The measured predictor is **biological sex**, recorded as Female or Male.
Gender is a distinct recorded construct; it is neither substituted for sex nor
entered in an H11 model. The estimand is the complete conditional Female-minus-
Male difference in `log10(30-minute arithmetic-mean melEDI + 0.1 lx)` across
the 48 observed half-hour clock-bin midpoints, equally averaged over the fixed
included site support. Near eye is primary; chest is complementary.

The final model uses the H02 clock-time, participant/day hierarchy, site
deviation, AR(1), boundary, and diagnostic decisions without reselecting them.
The observation is the analysis unit and participant is the independent
inference cluster. Results are associational and conditional on the included
sites.

## Exact fitted samples

The accepted main samples reconcile exactly to H02: 141 participants, 816
participant-days, and 37,756 half-hour observations at 9 sites near eye; and
154 participants, 902 participant-days, and 41,842 observations at 8 sites at
the chest. The sex join lost no fitted row.

```{r}
#| label: exact-samples
#| echo: false

samples |>
  mutate(
    Analysis = run_label(.data$run_id)
  ) |>
  select(
    Analysis,
    Participants = participants,
    Female = female_participants,
    Male = male_participants,
    `Participant-days` = participant_days,
    `30-minute observations` = observations_30_minute,
    `Nominal hours` = nominal_observation_hours,
    Sites = sites
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Exact fitted-model samples",
    "Female and Male columns are participant counts; nominal hours equal half the observation count."
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(
    Participants, Female, Male, `Participant-days`,
    `30-minute observations`, Sites
  )) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Nominal hours`, decimals = 1)
```

## Exact model and accepted inference

### Wilkinson formulas supplied to the fits

The following evaluated objects are the exact formulas supplied to `mgcv`.
`M_pattern` was used for all four final fREML fits. `M0` was fitted only for
the two main-placement descriptive effect-size branches after their global
tests opened those branches.

```{r}
#| label: exact-mpattern-formula
#| code-summary: "Exact final H11 formula"

cat(h11_formula_text(formulas$proposed_mpattern), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: exact-effect-baseline-formula
#| code-summary: "Exact conditional effect-size baseline formula"

cat(h11_formula_text(formulas$proposed_m0), "\n")
```

Both use Gaussian identity-link `bam()` fits with `method = "fREML"`,
`discrete = TRUE`, cyclic knots at 0 and 24 hours, and one run-specific rho
estimated from a rho-zero preliminary full model. Male is the treatment-
contrast reference. `sex_smooth` is the same biological-sex field ordered Male
then Female, yielding one cyclic Female-minus-Male deviation.

```{r}
#| label: fitted-model-map
#| echo: false

models |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = run_label(.data$run_id),
    Stage = recode(
      .data$model_id,
      mpattern_preliminary_rho0_fREML = "Preliminary full model, rho = 0",
      mpattern_final_fREML = "Final full model, accepted rho"
    ),
    Method = .data$method,
    Discrete = .data$discrete,
    `Elapsed (seconds)` = .data$elapsed_seconds,
    `Checkpoint reused` = .data$checkpoint_reused,
    Converged = .data$convergence
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Durable core fits",
    "The obsolete ML/discrete = FALSE comparison branch produced no accepted checkpoint and is not part of inference."
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Elapsed (seconds)`, decimals = 1)
```

### Participant-cluster-robust curve test

The global null is that the complete Female-minus-Male curve is zero at all 48
clock-bin midpoints. From each final `M_pattern` fit, the accepted method:

1. applies the run-specific AR(1) whitening transformation to the design and
   residuals, resetting at every accepted H02 `AR.start` boundary;
2. sums scores across all rows and days within participant;
3. forms a participant-cluster CR1 sandwich covariance and adds the `mgcv`
   smoothing-bias component `Vp - Ve`; and
4. uses the `mgcv` fractional-rank Wald statistic with finite-cluster F
   reference and denominator degrees of freedom
   `participants - ceiling(reference rank)`.

This is H11-METHOD-001 through H11-METHOD-007. It replaces, outcome-aware,
the unfinished ML/AIC branch. There is no delta-AIC support rule.

Multiplicity is fixed before display: one global test per placement or
sensitivity run (`planned n = 1`), and BH adjustment across the two planned
level/shape decomposition tests within each run (`planned n = 2`). Raw and
adjusted p-values below are labelled and formatted independently. Bold raw
p-values meet the raw 0.050 rule; bold adjusted p-values meet the separately
labelled adjusted 0.050 rule.

## Primary and complementary results

The complete near-eye Female-minus-Male curve test is supported
($F = `r sprintf("%.2f", primary_global$test_statistic)`$,
fractional numerator df = `r sprintf("%.2f", primary_global$test_df)`,
denominator df = `r primary_global$denominator_df`, raw p =
`r format_p_inline(primary_global$p_raw, primary_global$p_raw < 0.050)`,
BH-adjusted p =
`r format_p_inline(primary_global$p_adjusted_BH, primary_global$p_adjusted_BH < 0.050)`).
The complementary chest curve test is also supported
($F = `r sprintf("%.2f", chest_global$test_statistic)`$,
fractional numerator df = `r sprintf("%.2f", chest_global$test_df)`,
denominator df = `r chest_global$denominator_df`, raw p =
`r format_p_inline(chest_global$p_raw, chest_global$p_raw < 0.050)`,
BH-adjusted p =
`r format_p_inline(chest_global$p_adjusted_BH, chest_global$p_adjusted_BH < 0.050)`).

```{r}

#| echo: false

  transmute(
    Analysis = run_label(.data$run_id),
    `F statistic` = .data$test_statistic,
    `Numerator df` = .data$test_df,

  fmt_integer(columns = `Denominator df`) |>

```

The predeclared decomposition does **not** isolate a supported level or shape
component after BH adjustment. For near eye, the shape raw p is **0.043** but
its BH-adjusted p is 0.075; for chest, the level raw p is **0.029** but its
BH-adjusted p is 0.057. These raw values are styled under the separately
labelled raw 0.050 rule but are not substituted for the adjusted decomposition
decision.

```{r}

#| echo: false

comparisons |>
  filter(

    Component = recode(
      .data$comparison_id,
      parametric_level_component = "Constant level",
      cyclic_shape_component = "Cyclic shape"
    ),

    `Numerator df` = .data$test_df,
    `Denominator df` = .data$denominator_df,
    `Raw p` = .data$raw_p_display,
    `BH-adjusted p` = .data$adjusted_p_display,
    Decision = "Not supported after BH"
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Level/shape decomposition",
    "BH adjustment is applied within each two-test placement family. Raw and adjusted values are styled independently."
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(`F statistic`, `Numerator df`), decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = `Denominator df`) |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = c(`Raw p`, `BH-adjusted p`))
```

### Primary near-eye curves and pointwise intervals

All curve intervals are participant-cluster-robust **pointwise 95% confidence
intervals** at the 48 displayed bin midpoints. They are not simultaneous over
the day. Contiguous pointwise exclusions are descriptive and cannot establish
a familywise-supported significant period.

The smallest primary Female-to-Male shifted-value ratio occurs at
`r format_clock_midpoint(primary_minimum$time_hour)` and is
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary_minimum$female_to_male_shifted_ratio)`
(pointwise 95% CI
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary_minimum$ratio_lower_pointwise_95)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary_minimum$ratio_upper_pointwise_95)`). The largest is
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary_maximum$female_to_male_shifted_ratio)` at
`r format_clock_midpoint(primary_maximum$time_hour)` (pointwise 95% CI
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary_maximum$ratio_lower_pointwise_95)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary_maximum$ratio_upper_pointwise_95)`). These local
summaries do not replace the global test.

## Conditional biological-sex effect sizes

The author-approved gate opens within a main placement when its one-test global
robust raw p-value is below 0.050. It opened for near eye (raw p = **0.028**)
and chest (raw p = **0.029**), so an H02-like `M0` baseline was fitted under
fREML/discrete and exactly 50 hierarchical resamples were run as the authorised
pilot. No effect-size baseline was fitted for the sensitivity datasets.

The prediction-based estimates are very small. They are descriptive in-sample
relevance measures on the transformed response scale, not causal effects,
cross-validated prediction, or a unique partition of observed variance. A
small negative chest increment can occur because the baseline and full models
were smoothed separately under fREML; it indicates a negligible descriptive
increment rather than negative variance explained.

```{r}
#| label: effect-size-pilot
#| echo: false

effect_pilot |>
  filter(.data$effect_size_id %in% c(
    "sex_block_allocated_R2",
    "sex_block_share_of_full_R2",
    "sex_block_partial_R2"
  )) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = placement_label(.data$placement),
    Estimator = recode(
      .data$effect_size_id,
      sex_block_allocated_R2 = "Allocated in-sample R² increment",
      sex_block_share_of_full_R2 = "Share of full-model R²",
      sex_block_partial_R2 = "Partial R²"
    ),
    Estimate = .data$estimate,
    `Pilot 95% interval` = sprintf(
      "%.6f to %.6f",
      .data$pilot_lower_95,
      .data$pilot_upper_95
    ),
    Resamples = .data$bootstrap_replicates
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Conditional H02-like biological-sex effect-size pilot",
    "PILOT ONLY: 50 hierarchical resamples; intervals are not approved for inference or manuscript reporting."
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = Estimate, decimals = 6) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = Resamples)
```

```{r}
#| label: curve-variation-effect-size
#| echo: false

effect_variation |>
  transmute(
    Placement = placement_label(.data$placement),
    Estimate = .data$estimate,
    `Robust delta-method 95% CI` = sprintf(
      "%.4f to %.4f",
      .data$lower_95,
      .data$upper_95
    ),
    Unit = .data$unit,
    Role = "Conditional descriptive effect size; not variance explained"
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Equal-clock fitted-curve variation across biological sex",
    "The two sex curves are equally weighted over the 48 displayed clock bins."
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = Estimate, decimals = 4)
```

The 50-resample pilot took 0.061 seconds near eye and 0.066 seconds at the
chest. Linear projection from this fixed-prediction resampling gives 2.44
seconds (upper planning estimate 3.66 seconds) and 2.64 seconds (upper 3.96
seconds), respectively, for 2,000 resamples. These timings do not include
model refits because the approved estimator resamples stored fixed predictions.
A production run still requires explicit approval.

## Gap-timing-unaware sensitivity

The **gap-timing-unaware dataset** still passed the general 50%-per-hour and
80%-per-day coverage rules. “Gap-timing-unaware” means that the timing of the
remaining missing observations is not used for metric-specific adjustment.
For contrast in this first explanation only, the primary dataset could be
interpreted as a **time-sensitive primary metric dataset**. From here onward it
is called simply the primary dataset, while this sensitivity remains the
gap-timing-unaware dataset.

The global conclusion is stable. Near eye gives raw p = **0.026** and
BH-adjusted p = **0.026** on the gap-timing-unaware dataset, versus raw p =
**0.028** and BH-adjusted p = **0.028** on the primary dataset. Chest gives raw
p = **0.037** and BH-adjusted p = **0.037**, versus raw p = **0.029** and
BH-adjusted p = **0.029**, respectively. After holding the accepted model and
robust inference fixed, the primary preparation adds 7 near-eye participant-
days and 153 observations, and 8 chest participant-days and 178 observations.

```{r}
#| label: preparation-comparison
#| echo: false

preparation_comparison |>
  transmute(
    Placement = placement_label(.data$placement),
    `Primary participants` = .data$participants__main,
    `Primary participant-days` = .data$participant_days__main,
    `Gap-timing-unaware participant-days` =
      .data$participant_days__manuscript_prepared_data,
    `Added days` = .data$added_participant_days_main_minus_manuscript,
    `Added observations` = .data$added_observations_main_minus_manuscript,
    `Primary raw p` = styled_p(.data$p_raw__main, .data$p_raw__main < 0.050),
    `Gap-timing-unaware raw p` = styled_p(
      .data$p_raw__manuscript_prepared_data,
      .data$p_raw__manuscript_prepared_data < 0.050
    ),
    Stability = ifelse(
      .data$support_status__main == .data$support_status__manuscript_prepared_data,
      "Stable",
      "Changed"
    )
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Data-preparation comparison with inference held fixed",
    "Bold raw p-values meet the explicitly labelled raw 0.050 rule."
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(
    `Primary participants`, `Primary participant-days`,
```

The same-frame comparison separates model/inference changes from preparation
changes. On the gap-timing-unaware frame, replacing V0's separately estimated-
rho fREML AIC comparison and omitted parametric sex level with the accepted
joint robust test changes the chest conclusion from unsupported (V0 raw p =
0.414) to supported (raw p = **0.037** and BH-adjusted p = **0.037**). Near eye
remains supported, but its accepted raw p = **0.026** and BH-adjusted p =
**0.026** replace the decision-invalid V0 raw p = &lt;0.001. Moving from the gap-
timing-unaware frame to the primary frame then preserves both accepted
conclusions; that second change is attributable to data preparation.

```{r}
#| label: v0-comparison-near-eye
#| echo: false

v0_comparison |>
  filter(.data$placement == "glasses") |>
  transmute(
    Layer = .data$comparison_layer,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    Observations = .data$observations_30_minute,
    `V0 ΔAIC` = .data$delta_AIC_reduced_minus_full,
    `Robust F` = .data$test_statistic,
    `Raw p` = styled_p(
      .data$p_raw,
      .data$support_status == "supported" & .data$p_raw < 0.050
    ),
    Status = recode(
      .data$support_status,
      reopened_not_decision_valid = "V0 reopened; not decision-valid",
      supported = "Supported"
    ),
    Attribution = .data$change_attributed_to
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Near-eye V0, model/inference, and preparation comparison",
    "The V0 raw p-value is not bolded because that row is not decision-valid."
```

## Model and robust-inference diagnostics

All four final models are **acceptable with specified limitations**. Each
converged without a serious warning, the Female and Male cyclic curves close at
midnight, the inherited site deviations satisfy their sum-to-zero constraint,
and no severe basis-dimension flag was found. The accepted boundary-aware AR(1)
step reduced final lag-1 residual correlation to 0.083 near eye and 0.070 at
the chest on the primary dataset.

Residual tails remain heavier than Gaussian, absolute residual size is related
to fitted level, and the rich site/participant/day smooth structure remains
concurved. These are inherited H02 limitations. Participant-cluster robust
inference protects the sex test against heteroskedasticity, non-Gaussian score
variance, and residual dependence remaining within participants, but it does
not make the conditional mean model causal or generalise beyond the fixed site
support.

```{r}
#| label: diagnostic-assessments
#| echo: false

assessment |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = run_label(.data$run_id),
    Classification = .data$classification,
    Converged = .data$converged,
    `Warnings absent` = .data$serious_warning_absent,
    `Cyclic closure` = .data$cyclic_sex_curves_close_at_midnight,
    `Site constraint` = .data$site_sum_to_zero_verified,
    `Final lag-1 correlation` = .data$final_boundary_aware_lag1_correlation,
    `Severe k flags` = .data$severe_k_check_flags
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Explicit diagnostic assessment",
    "Acceptability is assessed per final fitted run, not inferred from convergence alone."
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Final lag-1 correlation`, decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = `Severe k flags`)
```

The robust covariance checks also pass. The tiny negative minimum eigenvalues
are numerical zero; the largest participant contributes 2.8% of unscaled meat
near eye and 7.5% at chest. Recomputing the coefficient-held-fixed sandwich
after deleting each participant keeps every main global p-value below 0.050.
This is an influence diagnostic, not a leave-one-participant model refit.

```{r}
#| label: robust-diagnostics
#| echo: false

robust_diagnostics |>
  filter(.data$run_id %in% c(primary_run, chest_run)) |>
  transmute(
    Placement = placement_label(.data$placement),
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `Reference rank` = .data$sex_block_reference_df,
    `Denominator df` = .data$denominator_df,
    `Largest participant meat share` =
      .data$maximum_participant_unscaled_meat_share,
    `Effective participants (trace)` =
      .data$effective_participants_unscaled_meat_trace,
    `Delete-one p range` = sprintf(
      "%.3f–%.3f",
      .data$delete_one_participant_p_minimum,
      .data$delete_one_participant_p_maximum
    ),
    `Minimum covariance eigenvalue` =
      .data$covariance_minimum_eigenvalue,
    `Context runtime (seconds)` =
      .data$robust_context_elapsed_seconds
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Participant-cluster robust-inference diagnostics",
    "Delete-one values recompute the sandwich with coefficients held fixed; they are not model refits."
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(`Reference rank`, `Effective participants (trace)`),
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(Participants, `Denominator df`)) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = `Largest participant meat share`, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = `Minimum covariance eigenvalue`, decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Context runtime (seconds)`, decimals = 1)
```

## Paired placement display applicability (REPORT-009)

An H05-style near-eye-on-x/chest-on-y identity scatter is **not valid** for
these Stage 2 temporal results. The accepted all-available fits use different
samples (141 versus 154 participants; 37,756 versus 41,842 observations), and
there is no predeclared scalar temporal estimand. Although stored H02 paired
frames exist for 112 participants, 643 participant-days, 29,786 matched
observations, and 8 sites, no H11 model has been fitted to those paired frames.
Fitting one solely to create the plot is prohibited.

The closest valid display is therefore the separate primary near-eye and
complementary chest curve panels above, with their exact samples stated and no
claim of equivalence or placement agreement. **No paired source-data CSV is
created** because no valid paired H11 fitted estimands exist at this stage.

```{r}
#| label: paired-display-assessment
#| echo: false

paired_display |>
  transmute(
    `Stored paired participants` = .data$stored_paired_frame_participants,
    `Stored paired participant-days` = .data$stored_paired_frame_participant_days,
    `Stored paired observations` = .data$stored_paired_frame_observations,
    `H11 paired fitted outputs` = .data$h11_paired_fitted_outputs_available,
    `Scalar identity plot applicable` = .data$scalar_identity_plot_applicable,
    `Paired source-data CSV` = ifelse(
      is.na(.data$paired_source_data_csv),
      "Not created",
      as.character(.data$paired_source_data_csv)
    )
  ) |>
  audit_gt(
    "REPORT-009 applicability assessment",
    "Unmatched all-available placement results are not plotted against each other."
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(
    `Stored paired participants`, `Stored paired participant-days`,
    `Stored paired observations`
  ))
```

## Interpretation

The accepted analysis supports an association between recorded biological sex
and the complete conditional temporal melEDI curve in the primary near-eye
data. Complementary chest evidence points in the same global direction. The
near-eye curve difference varies descriptively over clock time, whereas the
chest difference is estimated as almost constant, but the planned BH-adjusted
decomposition does not isolate either level or shape as a supported component.
Pointwise intervals contextualise the curves; they do not identify a
familywise-significant clock-time period.

The effect-size pilot indicates that the biological-sex block adds negligible
in-sample fitted relevance despite a supported global curve test. That
combination is possible: a precisely estimated structured difference can be
statistically supported yet account for very little of the outcome's total
within- and between-person variation. The association is not causal and cannot
be generalised to a population of sites without the deferred site sensitivity.
